technical_and_design_decisions: Use a toggle-based API for capabilities (Enable/Disable pattern) as suggested in U5, rather than allowing arbitrary capability strings
Add all new functions to the existing configtx/config (or equivalent) API package, following the established patterns for config manipulation helpers
Reuse the existing ConfigUpdate computation helper rather than re-implementing it, so each new function simply produces a writable in-memory config that can be passed to it
For U3, accept an org type enum (application, orderer, consortium) so a single function can retrieve policies for any org type
For U4, return a single config.Capabilities struct that exposes the three capability groups (application, orderer, channel) as fields, rather than three separate accessor functions
For U6, return the existing config.Application struct so the caller can drill into organizations, ACLs, capabilities, etc. without further parsing
For U7, provide symmetric Add/Remove ACLs functions that take a resource name and a policy reference, mirroring the pattern used elsewhere in the config API

For U8, split the monolithic example into five focused example tests (orderer config, application config, org management, MSP, capabilities) while keeping the existing end-to-end example as an integration test
Treat each user story as an independently reviewable/mergeable change to keep diffs small
assumptions: The target language is Go (consistent with the Hyperledger Fabric / configtxgen codebase)
The configtxgen example test harness is the appropriate place for the example updates called out in U1, U2, U3, U4, U5, U7, and U8
Types such as config.Application, config.Capabilities, and config.Org already exist or can be trivially introduced as thin wrappers over the existing protos
The developer is already familiar with the Fabric common/config and common/configtx layers, so no ramp-up time is included
Underlying protos and the standard config update/signing flow are stable; this work does not require proto regeneration or consensus changes
No performance, scalability, or concurrency considerations are required beyond what the existing helpers already provide
Code review will surface only minor issues (naming, comments, small refactors) since the design is constrained by the existing API surface
No backports to prior release branches are required; this targets the current development branch only
The toggle design decision for capabilities (U5) is settled in favor of Enable/Disable pairs, avoiding the need for a separate design document

activities.activity_description: Review the existing configtx config API, identify the right location for each new helper, confirm the function signatures and return types implied by the user stories, and resolve the capabilities toggle vs. setter design decision (U5).
Implement a helper that adds an orderer endpoint to an orderer org's config group and produces a ConfigUpdate-ready config. Add the corresponding example to the configtxgen example test.
Implement a helper that removes an orderer endpoint from an orderer org's config group and produces a ConfigUpdate-ready config. Add the corresponding example to the configtxgen example test.

Implement a helper that returns the policy map for a named organization regardless of whether the org belongs to the application, orderer, or consortium group. Update the example test to demonstrate usage.
Implement a helper that returns the orderer, application, and channel capabilities from a config transaction as a single config.Capabilities value. Add a brief example to the example test.

Implement Enable/Disable helper pairs for application, orderer, and channel capabilities (V2_0 toggles) that mutate a config transaction in place. Update the example test to demonstrate enabling and disabling each capability group.
Implement a helper that returns the application configuration group as a config.Application struct, without requiring the caller to navigate the protos manually. Add a short example.

activities.activity_name: U7 - Implement application ACL add/remove helpers
activities.activity_description: Implement helpers to add and remove entries from the application group's ACLs map, mutating the config transaction in place. Update the example test to demonstrate both adding and removing an ACL resource.

activities.activity_name: U8 - Refactor example tests into focused cases
activities.activity_description: Split the existing monolithic end-to-end example into five focused examples covering orderer configuration (with orderer policies), application configuration (with application policies), organization management (orgs, anchor peers, orderer endpoints), MSP modifications, and capabilities. Keep the original example as an integration smoke test.
Add Go unit tests covering positive cases, missing-org errors, and idempotency/in-place mutation behavior for each new helper introduced in A2-A8.
Run the full configtxgen and configtx test suites locally and in CI, and fix any breakages introduced by the new helpers or the example refactor.
Add GoDoc comments to each new exported helper and brief inline comments where the config mutation is non-obvious, so the API is self-describing.
Address reviewer feedback (naming tweaks, minor refactors, test adjustments) across the new code and the refactored examples.
